newsitem.title: USA: California budget talks resume - governor.
newsitem.headline: California budget talks resume - governor.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson and leaders of the state Senate and Assembly will meet Friday in hope of ending the state's budget standoff.
Welfare reform legislation has been the major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating the state's spending plan for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1.
The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
Wilson and legislative leaders plan to negotiate Friday night and through the weekend, the governor's office said.
"They're going to go at it again," said Wilson spokesman Ron Low. "We'll see what happens."
Earlier this week, Wilson vetoed the welfare reform plan drafted by state Democrats.
Republicans contended that the Democratic plan would be too generous and far too expensive, costing taxpayers $1 billion more each year than the governor's own welfare plan.
The state's final budget was expected to be in the $67 billion to $70 billion range.
